title: SHRDLU development period completed
summary: Terry Winograd later documented that he developed SHRDLU at MIT between 1968 and 1970. SHRDLU was a natural-language conversation program operating with a simulated robot arm in a tabletop blocks world, where it could answer questions, carry out commands, and incorporate new facts about that world.
significance: The record preserves a source-backed 1970 endpoint for SHRDLU's documented development period while avoiding an unsupported exact completion day or a claim that 1970 was a public release date.

verification.note: Verified against Terry Winograd's own retrospective account, which states that he developed SHRDLU at MIT between 1968 and 1970 and describes its conversational and simulated blocks-world capabilities. Year precision is used only for the documented endpoint of that development range. No exact completion date, public-release date, development geography, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationships are inferred.
